_doc: The canonical map of the agent's architecture, measured on the code. Source: the code. This map is the one representation the others (the web's Technology pages, the operator's session player, the observability events) are aligned to. A test (tests/infrastructure/unit/test_the_architecture_map_matches_the_code.py) fails when a path stops existing, a model id leaves config/models.default.json, or a flow names a piece that is not here.

_schema._doc: Optional fields every reader may use; a reader that does not know one ignores it.
_schema.status: On a zone or a piece: absent = built and live; "retiring" = still in the code and still running for some sessions, being replaced (a diagram draws it dashed or apart, never as the current path).
_schema.dir: On a flow or a view edge: "a>b" (a sends to b), "b>a", or "both" (a call that goes and comes back). Absent on a flow = not stated yet; a flow's `a`/`b` order alone carries no direction.
_schema.planned: Top-level list: pieces whose mechanism is decided and not built yet. They have no `paths` (nothing to point at); `will_live_in` names where they will be, `replaces` the ids they take over. They never appear in `flows`; a view may draw them with status "decided".
_schema.views: Top-level map of named diagrams over the same ids: a frame (the big block), the pieces inside it (`inside`), aggregate boxes (`outside`; `in_frame: true` draws one inside the frame as a summarised part of it) and directed edges. An aggregate box names what it summarises: `stands_for` (zones or pieces of this map) and/or `paths` (code that exists). A view adds no piece: every id it names is a piece, an external, a planned item, a zone or one of its own boxes.

blocks.label: External — voice, models and the world

zones.name: The old turn — retiring
zones._doc: The previous turn pipeline (gate, brief, prompt, one model call, acts, close). It still runs for a session the conversation manager does not take, and is being replaced piece by piece. Three of its boxes stay because other doors use them: the Jev client (`f_jev`), self-knowledge (`f_self`) and the consent/consequence doors (`f_doors`).

zones.name: Agent DNA
zones._doc: The genome (V2-859): the factory genes every install starts from, and the learned layer that grows over the agent's life (action aliases, playbook routes). The user's own rules are personal and never heritable: they are the rules zone, drawn next to this one, not inside it.

zones.name: Conversation & turn manager
zones._doc: The turn: the ear closes his turn, the inbox orders his entries across channels, the manager runs one batch at a time with the model, the gateway is the only door to an effect, the mouth says. The package (`conversation/`) imports nothing of the engine; the host (`nucleo/conversation_host/`) puts the engine behind its ports: the guards in front of the ear, the action map's shortcut, the route of what is open, the declared reads and acts and their doors, the state readers, the voice and the chat wall.

pieces.name: Canvas · widgets
pieces._doc: Every app declares the state its face shows and REPORTS it through one door (`POST /widgets/{id}/state`, `widgets/state.py`): a store per mounted screen, the order ledger (an order is pending until that screen acks its revision), host facts only the body may write (`by: host`), a `static` face for an app no order can move. A move under his hand is adopted as his order through the app's own action (`state_adopt`). Players share one reporter protocol.

pieces.name: Presence · the face
pieces._doc: The agent's face and its reactions, drawn on the device with zero tokens; the camera's «look at me» runs on-device in a Web Worker. What the face just did and saw reaches the engine as gesture names (`face_recent`), read by self-knowledge.

pieces.name: Voice process
pieces._doc: `python -m voice.engine`, started and supervised by the body (V2-891): the LiveKit session (ear, VAD, STT, TTS) lives here; its brain is the body, reached over loopback. `ZAELAR_VOICE_EMBEDDED=1` keeps it a thread of the body.

pieces.name: Body ↔ voice loopback
pieces._doc: The two loopback routes: `POST /api/turn/stream` (one voice turn, NDJSON lines the voice process speaks as they arrive) and `POST /api/voice/child/events` (the session's facts, in order, replayed through the same handlers an embedded session registers).

pieces.name: Homeostasis
pieces._doc: The body measures its own loop (`loop_lag`) and names whose stall it was (engine · host · unknown); the shed ladder and the watchdog share one pressure band, and a new worker is held while the host stalls (`waiting_host`).

pieces.name: Peer turn
pieces._doc: A peer's turn on a cluster, composed by the connector itself: the system text as language data, the relationship capsule and the peer's words with the security trailer last, one call through the model client and its relay. Its only act is the errand its permission grants. With the conversation manager on, the turn enters it as an event and runs after his words.

pieces.name: A2A · agent-to-agent mail
pieces._doc: Your agent reaches your friends' agents (V2-866): a mailbox pulled on a cadence or on a signed wake push, discovery by hash with a mutual match, relationships, grants as rules rows, queries and live shares. All code, no model call; off until switched on.

pieces.name: Ear
pieces._doc: The ear runs behind a relay (`voice/engine/speech/relay.py`): the titular, then an OpenAI stand-in when it fails; a hung titular is watched by `relay_bound.py` (shadow by default — it says what it would do). Each metric is billed to the provider that produced it.

pieces.name: Switchboard
pieces._doc: Whose his words are, decided ONCE at the turn's gate, before the model: one board of the open processes (running, or a row waiting on him) and one decision per chunk. For process N the chunk is delivered there as he said it and Flash does not run; for none, Flash takes the turn. His stop for an open process ends its row through the one cancel door. Retiring as a decider in front of the model: the conversation manager reaches it only through its route port, until the model answers an open process by id itself.

pieces.name: Admission · brief
pieces._doc: Every reader of the brief's verdicts reads one act floor (`verdicts.to_act`); at VETO a sure verdict takes the place of the model's call when what enters leaves or deletes, and a send in the model's place is born asking. The words follow the act: calls and tags wait for the verdict (`route_by_verdict`).

pieces.name: Jev client
pieces._doc: Stays: other doors use it, whatever turn runs.

pieces.name: Door trips
pieces._doc: A question only one door reads is asked AT that door, after the model (a model call, an errand's portal, a leaving act's exit, a parked directive), on its own thread and merged into the turn's brief; the turn's one tier-1 trip, before the model, asks only what the turn reads (V2-887 step 8).

pieces.name: Prompt · cached prefix
pieces._doc: The byte-stable system prefix, then the tools (always-offered before state-gated): what the provider caches, identical whatever he says or has open (V2-889 F1).

pieces.name: Turn state message
pieces._doc: What is true THIS turn (screen, clock, errands, record), sent as a second system message just before his line (`builder.split_state`), so the cached prefix never moves (V2-889 F1). The open apps' state lines ride here: ONE line per app as it REPORTS it, never as it was ordered (`widgets/state_render.py`, headed by its legend, a bounded budget; the apps the turn names lead).

pieces.name: Model call
pieces._doc: Retiring with the old turn; its client (`nucleo/llm/fast_client.py`) stays: the conversation manager's model port calls it.

pieces.name: Self-knowledge
pieces._doc: What the agent knows about itself: `about_self` answers from ONE catalogue (`catalog.json` + the `self` language pack) and the live snapshot (one reader per truth: settings, connectors, widgets, the camera, the face). Stays: other doors use it, whatever turn runs.

pieces.name: Consent · consequence
pieces._doc: Stays: other doors use it, whatever turn runs.

pieces.name: Whisperer (off)
pieces._doc: Beside the conversation manager, OFF and with no subscriber (V2-942 W1): a deterministic gate over a closed request's verdicts, then a typed slot with no instruction field. When switched on in shadow it is only measured — `whisper` events, wired into no prompt (V2-889 F2).

pieces.name: Mouth
pieces._doc: The voice runs behind the same relay: titular, then the OpenAI stand-in; `relay_bound.py` bounds a titular that hangs (armed: switches the voice, with a cooldown; shadow: says so).

pieces.name: Event pump
pieces._doc: The one subscriber per source and the one router of an event: a row waiting for it, a claimant (an errand's thread), a rule subscribed to it, or nothing (the source's own handling). The router still lives under the old turn's folder and moves to `nucleo/events/`.

pieces.name: Dispatch
pieces._doc: A worker is admitted under the memory floor its declared pieces need (`workers/envelope.py`) — held with its reason (`waiting_room`, `waiting_host`, `waiting_voice`) otherwise.

pieces.name: Task rows
pieces._doc: The order's row (`nucleo/request/`): one row per intention. His real tasks are one queue in the same table (`nucleo/queue`), whose one writer applies the signals of the pulse, the owner and him (`queue/<what>`). A send is one Brain Worker task with one confirmation at its exit door (`request/send_errand`); its final line is the connector's receipt (`request/send_receipt.py`), said through the out-of-turn notices.

pieces.name: Circuit
pieces._doc: An act on a card is done when the app REPORTS it (`circuit/reported.py`): an order the app has not confirmed waits, then settles unverifiable — never «done».

pieces.name: Messages out — the send owner and the connectors' exit
pieces._doc: A message has one owner (`nucleo/send`): one draft, shown in its widget's box; his words or his hand on the box change it; one confirmation he heard, or his Send by gesture; it leaves through the connectors' one exit and ends on the connector's receipt. Each step is seen in the flow of the order that opened it.

pieces.name: Network agents · mesh call
pieces._doc: Asking a live agent of the MeshKore network for an errand: find (the Oracle) and ask; a declared skill is CALLED by its id (`mesh_call`) — one order, one thread, one engine-made key; the agent's questions reach him through the asker and his answers go back; a job it opens is followed by the pulse (`mesh_jobs`) under a `remote_job` row until its final; a step it hands back (a page to open) is done only on his yes. Free agents only by default; a priced skill is a deposit the account settles.

pieces.name: Ear — the turn arbiter
pieces._doc: His voice (the speech-to-text's words and end of turn, through the voice process's lossless lane) and his typed lines and buttons, each through the guards in front of the ear: a closed microphone, our own echo, «only my voice», the attention mode and the vault, which takes a secret out before anything reads it.

pieces.name: Inbox — one order across channels
pieces._doc: One order across channels for his entries, and the door of the world's events: an event the router already routed enters as an entry of its own kind, with its source's authority, never his; it runs after his words and its route is obeyed by the one body that obeys it. The conversation model is not asked about an event.

pieces.name: Composer — the prompt, each thing once
pieces._doc: The prompt, each thing once: a byte-stable prefix (who is who, the language, how it speaks, what it may read and do), the state as facts (memory's state, the widgets on screen, the tasks open), the conversation window and the batch.

pieces.name: Effect gateway — the only producer of effects
Mouth — say, and what was heard
pieces._doc: Says a reply by voice and on the chat wall, never over his open voice, and records what was heard of it; says the lines owed to him (the notices ledger) when it is free.

pieces.name: Manager — the turn: policy, focus, one run
pieces._doc: One run at a time per account: the policy table by kind of input, the batch to the model with the whole declared catalogue, its orders (reply, no_reply, the four stops), a repair round for a figure its evidence does not back, and every request closed exactly once. Its model is the fast model behind a relay.

pieces.name: Shortcut — a phrase the action map knows verbatim
pieces._doc: Before any model: an exact whole-utterance hit in the action map runs its direct act and the run closes with that origin; no hit, the model.

pieces.name: Route — what is open takes his words
pieces._doc: Before the model, after the shortcut: an open message draft reads his sentence against itself (its one owner), then an open process or a row waiting on him (the switchboard). Taken, its line is said; not taken, the model answers.

pieces.name: Reads and acts — the declared catalogue and its doors
pieces._doc: Every tool the model sees is declared data (`declared.json`): its schema, what it is for and the door it goes to. Reads pass the gateway (web search, a widget's content and actions, a state topic, memory, the agent itself); a local act is reserved and carried to the door that already does it (the canvas, a widget's declared action, a task, the agent's own settings, a widget's life); a message goes to its one owner and leaves only through the connectors' exit door. A process of his is answered by its id (`task_answer`); a memory is forgotten or corrected by its id after a recall gave it.

emitters._doc: Which piece an observability event comes from (`piece`), for modules the pieces' `paths` do not name. Read by observability/pieces.py: an exact file here beats a piece's own path; otherwise the deepest folder (here or in a piece's paths) wins. A value is a piece id, or {kind: piece, '*': default} where one module hosts several pieces. A module drawn nowhere stamps piece='unmapped' with its path — never a guess.

external.name: Claude · Anthropic
external._doc: The Brain Worker's optional first rung (the model table's `lead`): Claude itself through the Claude Code CLI, present only where its credential resolves; the titular below it takes over when it is absent or parked.

the voice turn enters the body

a door reached asks its question

a job followed to its final

_flows: Who talks to whom. `a`/`b` alone carry no direction; `dir` (see `_schema`) says it where it is stated. `uncaptured` = the flow exists in the code but leaves no event (e.g. the rules read into every prompt).

views._doc: Named diagrams drawn from this file by the web and the session player. Ids are the map's; boxes ending in a view are aggregates drawn without detail.

architecture.title: Zaelar — one engine on your machine
architecture._doc: The whole engine as one block: what it is made of inside, and the outside it talks to. Each inner box summarises a zone of this map; its own diagram has the detail.

apps.title: A widget — one folder, declared once
apps._doc: What a widget is and who reaches it: what it can do is declared in its manifest and read by every caller; one funnel applies its actions; its face reports what it shows.

data.py — its data; every action through one funnel

brainworkers.title: Tasks — one row, one Brain Worker
brainworkers._doc: Work that takes more than a turn: a row that holds its state, one worker session per task, resumable by id, its hands the engine's own doors, and one writer of its ending.

Events and your rules — a row resumed, a rule's stream worker

a harness, a model per call

cluster.title: A cluster — a peer's turn
cluster._doc: Another agent writes on a cluster: the connector frames the peer's words as untrusted data, enters the turn into the conversation manager as an event after your words, and composes the reply itself. Tools only by a permission you granted.

outside.label: MeshKore network — the peer's agent
Conversation manager — the turn enters as an event, after your words
The model — one call, with its stand-in
An errand — only if a permission you granted allows it
Relationship memory — per cluster and peer, kept apart
You — grant a permission, set its objective

agent-to-agent mail: a mailbox, not a socket

memory.title: Memory — one entry, one writer
memory._doc: What is remembered and how it comes back: your words filed by the memory's own writer, a state always in the prompt as facts, recall on demand, and a sleep that consolidates.

outside.label: Conversation manager — your words filed, the state as facts, recall when asked, forget or correct by id

The file — memories, vectors, text index, graph, state, the vault

send.title: A message — from your order to its receipt
send._doc: A message has one owner (`nucleo/send`): one draft, shown in its widget's box; seven declared steps (`nucleo/send/steps.json`), each seen in the flow of the order that opened it; nothing leaves before his yes, by voice to the confirmation he heard or by his Send on the box; one exit with a lane per road and a hold switch; the connector's own receipt ends it.

not_drawn.config: settings and the model table (config/models.default.json): read by every piece, not a station a signal crosses
not_drawn.i18n: the strings every surface speaks in
not_drawn.update: the update channel: off the agent's hot path by design
not_drawn.observability: adds who/when/flow to the event log — the instrument the player reads, not a piece of the brain

_relays: Modules that CARRY the event stream: an event passes through them and is never from them (observability/pieces.py reads the first frame outside these as the emitter). `conversation/guard.py` is one: the events a transaction held are said when its timed store closes it, from the frame of whoever opened it.
